country.comment: Conducted in George Compound, a peri-urban settlement in Lusaka, Zambia.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title, Abstract, and Introduction; PDF p. 5, Section 3.3.1

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative phenomenological/case study; no quantitative point estimates, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Stakeholders reported that women's exclusion from household and community sanitation decision-making, non-involvement of absentee landlords, lack of flexible/instalment payment options for upfront toilet construction capital costs, utility billing by LWSC despite erratic or absent water supply, shallow pit latrine design with poor site planning/demarcation, and low community awareness/compliance with sanitation laws despite inspectorate enforcement hindered equitable and sustainable on-site sanitation and water access in George Compound, Lusaka.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 7–10, Sections 4.1.1–4.4.6; PDF pp. 10–13, Sections 5.1–5.4 and Conclusion

mechanism_certainty.comment: Primary qualitative study (appraised with CASP Qualitative Checklist, design ceiling = 2) that directly documents institutional, financial, landlord-tenure, planning, and participatory barriers operating on household on-site sanitation and water access via interviews with beneficiaries, local committees, regulators, and the utility.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 5–7, Sections 3.2–3.5; PDF pp. 7–11, Sections 4.1–5.2

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines women's participation/exclusion in sanitation committees and decision-making (participation), upfront toilet construction costs and billing without water delivery alongside calls for flexible instalment plans (fees, accommodation), absentee landlord non-involvement and tenant reliance on landlords for toilets (tenure, property), poor demarcation/planning in unplanned peri-urban settlements and construction permit/code context (planning, building_permit), regulatory/inspectorate compliance gaps and fines (sanction), and involvement of political leaders and local authorities in advocacy/sensitisation (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, participation, fees, accommodation, tenure, property, planning, building_permit, sanction, political_coordination
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 4, Background; PDF pp. 7–12, Sections 4.1.1–4.4.6 and 5.1–5.4; PDF p. 13, Conclusion

outcome_flags.comment: Examines household on-site toilet construction and shared latrine access (sanitation_access), water supply for household and toilet/menstrual hygiene use (water_access), shallow pits filling rapidly and unhygienic facilities (service_quality), erratic water supply, opening hours/long queues, and borehole disruptions from electricity load-shedding (service_reliability, service_continuity), and inability to afford upfront toilet capital costs plus spending household income buying water while billed by LWSC (affordability).
outcome_flags.value: sanitation_access, water_access, service_quality, service_reliability, service_continuity, affordability
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 8–9, Sections 4.1.1–4.1.2; PDF p. 13, Conclusion

publication_year.comment: Published in Volume IX Issue XI November 2025, with explicit publication date 25 December 2025.
publication_year.where_found: PDF p. 1, journal header and publication date line

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary qualitative study using in-depth interviews and key informant interviews analysed with Braun and Clarke reflexive thematic analysis.

sample_size.comment: Section 3.3.3 states '29 Participants (10 Males and 15 women) and 4 key informants' determined by data saturation; note that 10 males + 15 women = 25 community beneficiaries plus 4 key informants = 29 total participants (though the sentence phrasing could also be read as 29 + 4 = 33 if the parenthetical was an arithmetic slip).
sample_size.value: 29 participants (reported as 10 males and 15 women [25 beneficiaries] and 4 key informants)

study_design.comment: Described in the title and Section 3.2 as a hermeneutic/interpretive phenomenological qualitative study and in the Conclusion (p. 12) as an exploratory single-case study, operationalized via criterion-based purposive sampling, in-depth interviews with beneficiaries, key informant interviews with institutional/community stakeholders, and reflexive thematic analysis.
study_design.value: Qualitative interpretive/hermeneutic phenomenological case study (in-depth interviews and key informant interviews analysed with reflexive thematic analysis)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF pp. 5–7, Sections 3.1–3.5; PDF p. 12, Conclusion
